summary: Readers no longer depend on a stored record for each valid replicated claim: a view (replica_record_rows) gives every reader the record each valid claim had, from its envelope and position, and the store is ready to delete valid replica records after a rollback window. The deletion itself ships switched off in this release

replay.detail: No replay. Readers that asked for a valid record (the self-writer and pairing signer checks, the desired-row and selector projection gates, the replication status count and the local trim capture) read the claim, its envelope by batch and its position instead, which give the same answers while every valid record is still stored.

schema.detail: Adds the view replica_record_rows and the table record_repair_lookups (empty unless a repair waits for a deleted record). DELETE triggers on replica_records (completion health, resource preparation, custom, glass heads, directive notes, publication and the IVM sources) fire only for a record that is not valid, replaced in place when their definition differs. Readers accept storage version 23 (MAX_SUPPORTED_STORAGE_VERSION 23); nothing in this release writes it. New config [store] valid_record_delete_after (3d unless set) for the deletion that a later release switches on.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rule or fleet coordination change.

compatibility.detail: No wire or API change. Peers exchange the same envelopes.

downtime.detail: No startup work beyond creating the view and table and replacing the changed triggers in the opening transaction.

recovery.detail: Rollback to the previous release is supported: valid records are still stored and the store stays at storage version 20. The previous release recreates its own trigger definitions on open. When a later release switches deletion on, its first deletion commits storage version 23, which the previous release refuses; that release's note states the floor.
